name: Eibsee I
bestFor: Lakes, coastlines and rough water under gray skies, in the Alps or on northern coasts.
whatItDoes: The Stetten I base with dehaze pulled to -13 for a softer, misty feel, and yellows slightly desaturated and brightened.
watchOut: Negative dehaze takes more contrast out of already foggy frames.

name: Grainau I
bestFor: Alpine meadows, lone trees and lakeside forest in daylight.
whatItDoes: The shared base with vibrance cut and saturation raised, which pushes strong colors further while holding muted ones back. Yellows lean green.

name: Seiser Alm I
bestFor: Alpine meadows with peaks behind them and green paths in soft light.
whatItDoes: The shared base with vibrance cut and saturation up, and yellows shifted toward green and brightened for vivid grass.
watchOut: Close to Grainau I, with a stronger yellow shift (+43) that makes grass greener.

name: Zugspitze I
bestFor: Peaks lit at sunrise or sunset, alpine chapels and summit crosses.
whatItDoes: The shared base with a vibrance lift and greens shifted toward yellow, desaturated and brightened for pale spring grass. Yellows lean green and brighten.
watchOut: Forest goes pale and yellowish. Grainau I keeps greens deeper.

name: Vienna I
bestFor: Palaces, formal gardens, gothic spires and lake views under overcast skies.
whatItDoes: The shared base with deeper blacks and a large green-primary hue shift in calibration.
watchOut: The calibration shift (+88) changes every green. Check foliage frame by frame.

name: Allgäu I
bestFor: Green pastures, mountain lakes and single trees under big skies.
whatItDoes: Stetten II's color with near-maximum highlight recovery (-95), shadows at +76 and a slight dehaze boost. It keeps an AI sky mask and two gradient masks.
watchOut: The gradients sit where they were on the original frames. Reposition or delete them.

name: Salzburg I
bestFor: Church and cathedral interiors and autumn paths where deep shadows need opening.
whatItDoes: The shared base with shadows near the maximum (+84), a warm midtone grade, and aquas and blues muted. Grain 19.

name: Hallstatt I
bestFor: Lakeside village views framed by foliage, in mist or overcast.
whatItDoes: The base color with a strong shadow lift, a dehaze cut, greens shifted further and heavily desaturated, and green primary saturation raised in calibration.

name: Mount Rainier II
bestFor: Hazy or overcast mountain days where the green slopes need to stand out from a pale sky. Also works on mountain village streets.
whatItDoes: Adds contrast and color, recovers bright skies, tints shadows blue and highlights warm, and shifts yellow-greens toward a cooler green.

name: Hopfensee II
bestFor: Misty lakes, alpine villages and wooden houses in morning haze.
whatItDoes: More contrast (+38) and vibrance (+45) than Hopfensee I, blues and aquas left nearly at full saturation, and reds shifted slightly toward magenta.

name: Stetten I
bestFor: Green countryside, vineyards and village views in daylight, including shots framed through gates or windows.
whatItDoes: The shared base look (softened texture and clarity, faded blacks, blue shadows, warm highlights, light grain) with shadows opened wide and greens and yellows made brighter and more saturated.
watchOut: Greens get loud fast on already lush scenes. Pull Green saturation back if grass starts to glow.

name: Mount Fremont I
bestFor: Bright, high-contrast scenes where the sky would otherwise blow out. It is built on Mount Rainier II, so it suits the same mountain scenes.
whatItDoes: Mount Rainier II with full highlight recovery and much more vibrance.
watchOut: The extra vibrance makes saturated clothing loud. Lower Vibrance if reds run hot.

name: Lago di Braies II
bestFor: Turquoise mountain lakes and the trails around them.
whatItDoes: Recovers bright skies, lifts shadows, shifts aqua water toward blue and deepens it. No grain, so it stays clean.
watchOut: Magenta is fully desaturated, so pink flowers or clothing turn gray.

name: Lofoten I
bestFor: Rock, weathered wood, fishing gear and other textured subjects in overcast light.
whatItDoes: Heavy texture (+28) and clarity (+48) with a faded curve that lifts blacks hard. No HSL changes.
watchOut: This is the strongest clarity in the library. Keep it off faces and noisy skies.

name: Salzburg II
bestFor: Golden-hour town and lakeside views, fortresses and stone archways.
whatItDoes: More contrast and less shadow lift than Salzburg I, darker yellows, muted aquas and blues, and the red primary shifted toward orange and desaturated in calibration.
watchOut: Red flowers and signs go dull from the red primary cut.

name: Vienna II
bestFor: Candlelit interiors, church naves and stained glass in warm low light.
whatItDoes: The Rome II color base with light highlight recovery, a dehaze cut, oranges muted and brightened, much brighter yellows, more vibrance and saturation, and lighter grain (21).
watchOut: The light highlight recovery lets bright windows and flames clip.

name: Lofoten II
bestFor: Arctic harbors, snowy peaks and open sea under gray skies.
whatItDoes: The shared base with shadows at +100 and aquas and blues desaturated, so sea and sky read cold and quiet.

name: Kiruna II
bestFor: Arctic rivers, winter skies and buildings under heavy cloud, plus golden autumn birch.
whatItDoes: A strong shadow lift with a strong grade (blue shadows, warm highlights, warm midtone), and yellows and greens shifted, saturated and brightened for golden foliage.
watchOut: Nothing like Kiruna I. Yellows can go neon under artificial light.

name: Rome II
bestFor: Hillside villages, vineyards and canal houses in soft or overcast light.
whatItDoes: The second base family: softened texture and clarity, heavy grain (50), yellows pushed green and desaturated, greens muted, aquas and blues mostly drained, and a red calibration shift.

name: Bavaria I
bestFor: Misty lake villages, forest ponds and pale cathedrals in flat light.
whatItDoes: Rome II with lighter highlight recovery (-49) and vibrance cut to -13, so it is flatter and more muted.

name: Amsterdam II
bestFor: Tree-lined streets, canals and old buildings with greenery.
whatItDoes: Rome II with less highlight recovery (-57), saturation +35 and lighter grain (34).

name: Hoh Rainforest I
bestFor: Dense, shaded forest with moss, tall trunks and ferns.
whatItDoes: Softens texture and clarity, raises overall saturation while holding yellows and greens back so the forest stays deep green, and adds grain.
watchOut: Saturation is high, so red or pink flowers in the frame get very intense.

name: Neuschwanstein I
bestFor: Castles and villages seen from a viewpoint, with lakes and forest around them, including on overcast days.
whatItDoes: Raises saturation and vibrance while holding yellows and greens back, with a blue and warm split and light grain.

name: Mount Rainier I
bestFor: Green landscapes in soft or overcast light: pastures, hillsides and forest paths.
whatItDoes: Cuts yellow, green and orange saturation for muted greens, tints shadows teal, adds a red-magenta midtone grade and brightens reds.

name: Hallstatt III
bestFor: Misty lakes, rivers and lakeside towns on gray days.
whatItDoes: Brightens whites while pulling highlights far down, so fog and cloud keep their detail. Adds saturation, a blue and warm split, grain, and masks for sky, water and subject.

name: Kiruna I
bestFor: Snow and winter scenes that need almost no styling.
whatItDoes: Mild contrast, brighter whites and a vibrance lift. No grade, no grain, no HSL work.
watchOut: It is the lightest preset in the library, so it will not tie a set together the way the graded presets do.

name: Boston II
bestFor: Ornate interiors, period rooms and architectural detail.
whatItDoes: Boston I's color with gentler highlight recovery (-59), a larger dehaze cut, grain 25 and a slightly softer curve.
watchOut: Bright windows clip sooner than with Boston I.

name: Cary IV
bestFor: Night light displays where Cary III looks too cold.
whatItDoes: Cary III's hazy base plus a grade: blue shadows, green-teal highlights and a warm midtone.
